decision_reason: Exact-pin over all 11 fields of RecoveryRuntimeSummary via assert_eq! is the strongest behavior-test verification; risk_tags behavior-test+exact-pin require a unit-test/property-test gate on summarize_recovery_events to confirm the production derivation is stable across the fuzz payload shape. No proptest Arbitrary strategy is needed because the fuzz payload shape is constant (single RunAccepted, seq=EventSeq::new(1)); cargo test on the existing unit-test suite is sufficient.

Frame-seed call site (lines 201-203) is byte-identical pre/post fix; risk_tags behavior-test+noop require a unit-test gate on recover_runtime_frame_seed_from_events to confirm the no-op is preserved. Cargo test on the existing unit-test suite is the natural gate.

Compile + source-lint gate over the rewritten fuzz body. The cargo build --bin recovery_decode --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml gate (the fuzz/ directory is a separate Cargo workspace with package name velvet-ballistics-fuzz; --manifest-path is the canonical cross-workspace invocation) proves the new assert_eq!(RecoveryRuntimeSummary, RecoveryRuntimeSummary) compiles against the existing PartialEq+Eq+Copy+Debug derive set; the grep gate proves none of the C-8 forbidden patterns (assert!(* || *), matches!(*, ..), field-by-field chain, let _summary, dbg!, unwrap/expect) reappear in the non-empty branch. Risk_tags blast-radius-control + source-lint + forbidden-pattern demand a build-and-lint combination; cargo build + grep is the only available surface for this bead (no dedicated lint verifier is in the schema).

Defect is in test code, not production. Production RecoveryRuntimeSummary derives PartialEq+Eq+Copy+Debug at crates/vb_storage/src/recovery/types.rs:546 and summarize_recovery_events is unchanged; no new Rust-local invariant is introduced by the test-only fix. Per proof-seeds.jsonl PS-vb-vzo9b-1 notes: 'No Verus/Kani/Flux refinement needed because the production derivation is constant in this fuzz payload shape.'

Defect is in test code, not production. No new bounded symbolic claim is introduced; the fuzz payload shape is a single RunAccepted event with seq=EventSeq::new(1) and the assertion is over a Copy+PartialEq+Eq struct. Per proof-seeds.jsonl PS-vb-vzo9b-1 notes: 'cargo-test exact-pin is sufficient. No Verus/Kani/Flux refinement needed.' Kani's bounded symbolic exploration adds no unique evidence beyond cargo test on the existing recovery_unit_tests and replay/summary/tests.rs surface.

Defect is in test code, not production. No new refinement type is introduced; the fix is a plain assert_eq! over an existing Copy+PartialEq+Eq struct. RecoveryRuntimeSummary's field set is unchanged. Per delivery-scope.jsonl row 30: flux required=false. Per proof-seeds.jsonl PS-vb-vzo9b-1 notes: 'No Verus/Kani/Flux refinement needed.'

No concurrency, atomics, channels, locks, async shutdown, or task ownership in scope. The fuzz harness fuzz_recovery_decode is a synchronous function reading stdin bytes; production recovery functions called by it are single-threaded. fuzz/src/journal_target/readback.rs has no tokio, crossbeam, std::sync::*, or Send/Sync boundary in the touched surface.

All touched files carry #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; zero unsafe blocks, no FFI, no raw pointers, no MaybeUninit, no provenance-sensitive operations. The fuzz harness and the production recovery surface it calls all use safe Rust only.

The fuzz harness body is the target of the change, not a separate fuzz target. The repair tightens assertions inside the existing fuzz harness rather than introducing a new fuzz target. The contract C-7 closure commands explicitly list cargo build --bin recovery_decode --manifest-path fuzz/Cargo.toml and the two cargo test invocations, not a cargo fuzz run. The cargo-build lane (PO-003) covers the build/compile path that cargo-fuzz would otherwise exercise via libfuzzer's pre-build step.
